instruction: In the tomb at the top of the hill of [name], whose great front was begun but never freed from the rock: through the door cut between the stepped battlements, in the chamber, 2 cubits: [deposit].
context: Redacted site description: a necropolis of isolated sandstone hills in an oasis plain. Large tomb façades crowned with stepped battlements are cut into the hill faces; the recorders numbered the tombs hill by hill. The hill in question runs roughly north-south and is about 60 m high at its north end; its north-east face was left uncut because the lower rock crumbles.

position.relative_to: first tomb of the series, at the north-west end of the hill

features.notes: Where the series turns south. Unique decoration: over the door two animals face each other before a rosette.

position.relative_to: first tomb of the series, at the north-west end of the hill

features.opening: door at the foot of the façade
features.notes: Fifth in the series; one of three well-preserved façades side by side, each with an inscription in perfect state.

position.relative_to: first tomb of the series, at the north-west end of the hill

features.opening: door at the foot of the façade
features.dimensions: façade about 20 m high on a base 4-5 m high
features.notes: First tomb of the series; finished façade crowned with stepped battlements; a long dated inscription over the door, too high to be squeezed by earlier visitors.

position.relative_to: first tomb of the series, at the north-west end of the hill

features.opening: door at the foot of the façade
features.notes: On the western face; one of the last two façades of the series, among the finest of the site.

features.type: pit graves cut in the rock (group)
features.opening: open pits; reached by a rough stair cut between two small tombs
features.notes: A considerable number of graves dug into the rock surface on the hilltop.

position.relative_to: first tomb of the series, at the north-west end of the hill

features.opening: door at the foot of the façade
features.notes: Third large tomb in the series along the hill face; one of the finest façades; local tradition attaches a story to it.
